title: Affine-space cell and regular geometry of a general Borel quotient
statement: Let $F$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G$ be a smooth connected affine $F$-group scheme of finite type [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $B\subseteq G$ be a Borel subgroup: a maximal smooth connected solvable closed subgroup, where solvable means that successive derived subgroup schemes eventually become trivial, and the derived subgroup is the smallest closed subgroup through which the commutator morphism factors. Let $Q=G/B$ denote the $F$-scheme representing the fppf sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/B(A)$ on commutative $F$-algebras, where fppf coverings are jointly surjective flat finitely presented coverings. Then $Q$ is a regular [def-weil-regular-scheme], integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], Noetherian separated $F$-scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Here Noetherian means that $Q$ has a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings, and separated means that its diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is a closed immersion. There are an integer $n\geq0$ and a dense open subscheme $U\subseteq Q$ with an $F$-isomorphism $U\simeq\operatorname{Spec}F[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. No reductivity hypothesis on $G$ is imposed; $G=B$ and $n=0$ are allowed.

source.place: Lemma 18.21, printed p.392, proof: apply Proposition 13.52 (p.275) as in the proof of Theorem 17.65 (p.374). Quotient existence and smoothness: Theorem 7.18 and Remark 7.16(c), pp.142--143; completeness: Theorem 17.9, p.354. Only the regular Noetherian separated integral geometry and affine-space cell are retained.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry] with $H=B$. Its quotient represents exactly the fppf sheaf in the statement, so denote its canonical map by $q:G\to Q$. It gives $Q$ separated and of finite type over $F$, $q$ faithfully flat, and $G\times_F B\simeq G\times_QG$, $(g,b)\mapsto(g,gb)$. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $(0)$ and $(1)$; hence [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $Q$ Noetherian. Since $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is affine, [lem-sc-separated-over-affine-scheme-separated] gives the absolute separation required here; [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] gives that $Q$ is quasi-separated.

source.place: Theorem 7.18 and Propositions 5.24--5.25, printed pp.104--105 and 143; Stacks morphisms.tex Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian); schemes.tex Tags 01KN (lemma-affine-separated), 01KU (lemma-separated-permanence).

proof.text: Verify the quotient hypotheses needed in the next step. The composite $G\xrightarrow{q}Q\to\operatorname{Spec}F$ is of finite type, so [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target](a) makes $q$ locally of finite type. The Noetherian target $Q$ and [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth] make it locally of finite presentation. Since $G$ is affine and $Q$ quasi-separated, [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence](1) makes $q$ of finite presentation, including quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. It is therefore an fppf covering by itself. For any $F$-scheme $T$ and $x:T\to Q$, [lem-trf-fppf-covering-base-change] gives the fppf covering $T\times_QG\to T$, which is fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc]; its second projection to $G$ lifts $x$. For $a,b\in G(T)$ the fibre-product isomorphism of [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry] says $q(a)=q(b)$ exactly when $b=ah$ for some $h\in B(T)$, equivalently $a^{-1}b\in B(T)$. Thus $q$ has every quotient property in [lem-sfb-algebraic-group-homogeneous-quotient].

source.place: Stacks morphisms.tex Tags 01T8 (lemma-permanence-finite-type), 01TX (lemma-noetherian-finite-type-finite-presentation); schemes.tex Tags 03GI (lemma-quasi-compact-permanence), 01KV (lemma-compose-after-separated); topologies.tex Tags 021O (lemma-fppf), 022C (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc).

proof.text: Now apply [lem-sfb-borel-quotient-proper-geometry] to $H=B$, $X=Q$ and $p=q$. The group $G$ is smooth connected affine of finite type, and $B$ is smooth connected closed by the Borel hypothesis. Step 2 supplied faithful flatness, finite presentation, the coset equality on every test scheme and fpqc-local lifts. The cited statement therefore gives that $Q$ is regular, Noetherian and geometrically integral. Taking the field extension $F/F$ gives integrality. Together with the absolute separation in Step 1 these are all the asserted geometric properties.

source.place: Corollaries 5.26--5.27, printed p.105, Proposition 7.15, printed pp.142--143, and Theorem 17.9(a), printed p.354; regularity as in Stacks descent.tex Tag 036D (lemma-regular-local-smooth).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-general-flag-isolated-linear-action], choose $E$, an equivariant closed immersion $Q\hookrightarrow\mathbf P(E)$ and $\lambda:\mathbf G_m\to G$ with finite reduced fixed subscheme. Restrict the representation and the left action along $\lambda$. Since $Q$ is quasi-compact by Step 1, the closed immersion makes $Q$ projective by [def-pc-projective-morphism]. Step 3 gives that $Q$ is smooth and nonempty connected (it is integral), so [lem-sfb-projective-attracting-cells] applies with these data. Its open dense stratum $U$ is isomorphic to $\mathbf A_F^n$ for $n\geq0$. The affine-base clause of [def-sbc-affine-space] identifies this with $\operatorname{Spec}F[t_1,\ldots,t_n]$, as required.

source.place: Lemma 18.21, proof, p.392: apply Proposition 13.52, p.275, by its Theorem 13.47/Corollary 13.49 attracting-cell proof and the general-flag setup in the proof of Theorem 17.65, p.374.
